tasks.title: Understand a simple timetable
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: Le cours commence à neuf heures.
tasks.context:
Read
Le cours commence à neuf heures. La pause est à dix heures. Je regarde l’horaire et je demande : « À quelle heure est le cours ? »

Understand
Ask À quelle heure… ? for a time. À neuf heures means at nine o’clock. Learn le cours commence as a useful phrase. In this timetable, neuf heures is the start of class and dix heures is the break; keep the two details separate.

Model: Le cours commence à neuf heures.
Meaning: The class starts at nine o’clock.

Glossary
à neuf heures — at nine o’clock
une pause à dix heures — a break at ten o’clock
l’horaire du cours — the class timetable

tasks.title: Say a day and a date
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: Nous sommes le premier mai.
tasks.context:
Read
Nous sommes le premier mai. Dans cette situation imaginaire, c’est lundi. Mardi matin, je rencontre une amie. Je note le jour et la date dans mon agenda.

Understand
For the first day of a month, use le premier: le premier mai. Other dates generally use a cardinal number: le deux mai. French day and month names normally take a lower-case initial. The weekday in this passage is invented, not a statement about a real calendar year.

Model: Nous sommes le premier mai.
Meaning: It is the first of May.

Glossary

mardi matin — Tuesday morning
noter la date — to write down the date

tasks.title: Agree a familiar colour adjective
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: La veste est bleue.
tasks.context:
Read
Je regarde les vêtements. La veste est bleue. Le pantalon est noir. Les chaussures sont rouges. Je choisis la veste pour sortir.

Understand
A colour adjective such as bleu normally agrees with the noun: une veste bleue, un manteau bleu. Rouge already ends in e in both singular genders; add s for des chaussures rouges. This small set is not a rule for every colour word: some colour expressions are invariable.

Model: La veste est bleue.
Meaning: The jacket is blue.

Glossary
une veste bleue — a blue jacket
un pantalon noir — black trousers
des chaussures rouges — red shoes

tasks.title: Say what you do not have
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: Je n’ai pas de monnaie.
tasks.context:
Read
À la caisse, je cherche des pièces. Je n’ai pas de monnaie. Je demande : « Est-ce que je peux payer par carte ? » La personne répond oui.

Understand
With avoir, put ne/n’ before the verb and pas after it: je n’ai pas. An indefinite or partitive quantity often becomes de after negation: j’ai de la monnaie → je n’ai pas de monnaie. This is not a rule for every article or verb: je n’aime pas le café keeps le, and ce n’est pas un stylo keeps un.

Model: Je n’ai pas de monnaie.
Meaning: I do not have any change.

Glossary
de la monnaie — some change
chercher des pièces — to look for coins
payer sans espèces — to pay without cash

tasks.title: Locate an everyday place
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: La pharmacie est près de la gare.
tasks.context:
Read
Je cherche une pharmacie. La pharmacie est près de la gare. La boulangerie est en face du parc. Je regarde le plan avant de partir.

Understand
Où est… ? asks where something is. Près de means near. With de + le, use du: près du parc. With a feminine article, de la remains two words: près de la gare. A location is not a direction: près de says where a place is, not which way to turn.

Model: La pharmacie est près de la gare.
Meaning: The pharmacy is near the station.

Glossary
près de la gare — near the station
en face du parc — opposite the park
regarder le plan — to look at the map

tasks.title: Describe a morning with a familiar verb
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: Je me lève à sept heures.
tasks.context:
Read
Le matin, je me lève à sept heures. Je prends le petit déjeuner. À huit heures, je pars pour l’université. Le soir, je me couche tôt.

Understand
Learn je me lève as a complete present-tense expression meaning I get up. Me belongs to this pronominal verb with je; do not omit it. Compare je pars, where no me is needed. The verb lever changes its written vowel in je me lève. Start with this form before learning the whole pattern.

Model: Je me lève à sept heures.
Meaning: I get up at seven o’clock.

Glossary
se lever tôt — to get up early
prendre le petit déjeuner — to have breakfast
se coucher tard — to go to bed late

tasks.title: Use au, à la and aux with a destination
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: Je vais au marché.
tasks.context:
Read
Aujourd’hui, je vais au marché. Après, je vais à la bibliothèque. Un ami demande où sont les toilettes. Je montre le panneau.

Understand
With a destination and a definite article: à + le becomes au, à + les becomes aux, while à la stays separate. Compare au marché, à la bibliothèque, aux toilettes. These are not rules for every country/place expression; learn the current examples before adding other patterns.

Model: Je vais au marché.
Meaning: I am going to the market.

Glossary
au marché — to the market
à la bibliothèque — to the library
aux toilettes — to the toilets

Speak: retell the situation with an invented detail and ask the Tutor one follow-up question. Listen to the reply and request clarification if needed. Review the previous lesson model and your saved mistakes. Feedback is practice evidence, not CEFR certification.

tasks.title: Keep a conversation going when you do not understand
tasks.objective: Understand and use the target expression in a short everyday exchange: Pouvez-vous répéter, s’il vous plaît ?
tasks.context:
Read
Je ne comprends pas la phrase. Je demande : « Pouvez-vous répéter, s’il vous plaît ? » La personne parle plus lentement. Je dis merci et je vérifie un mot : « Comment ça s’écrit ? »

Understand
Pouvez-vous répéter… ? is a useful memorised request. Vous is polite or plural. A hyphen links pouvez and vous in this inverted question. Ask plus lentement for slower speech. Repetition and spelling are ways to repair communication, not signs that you must stop practising.

Model: Pouvez-vous répéter, s’il vous plaît ?
Meaning: Could you repeat, please?

Glossary
plus lentement — more slowly
je ne comprends pas — I do not understand
comment ça s’écrit — how is that spelled

Speak: retell the situation with an invented detail and ask the Tutor one follow-up question. Listen to the reply and request clarification if needed. Review the previous lesson model and your saved mistakes. Feedback is practice evidence, not CEFR certification.

tasks.title: Write a clear meeting message
tasks.objective: Give a day, time and place and ask for confirmation in a short message.
tasks.context: Write 30–50 French words to an imaginary classmate. Suggest a day, time and meeting place. Ask whether the arrangement is suitable. Include a greeting and closing. Use invented details, not personal addresses. Reread: are the day and time consistent, are the words spelled with accents, and is the request clear? Optional AI feedback is advisory; no automatic CEFR level is awarded.

tasks.title: Describe your day and solve one small problem
tasks.objective: Connect a simple routine with one practical request and a response.
tasks.context: Write 40–60 French words about an imaginary day. Give two routine activities and their times. Add one small problem, such as not understanding a word or needing a routine appointment, and write a polite request. Use language from earlier lessons. Check present verb forms, articles, negation and accents. Then read the text aloud and practise a follow-up with the Tutor. Feedback is advisory; transcription is not pronunciation scoring.
